director_mandate.binding_question_summary: On the credential-free GET-only stdlib-HTTP substrate, over a frozen multi-host pool confirmed during DESIGN by a pre-freeze attainability certificate to contain DEEP (hop>=3) state-carrying items on at least two distinct hosts/engines, does site-native discovery (robots.txt/sitemap, on-site search, RSS/Atom, JSON-LD enumeration) let a fresh agent reach those DEEP items in O(1) GETs (K<=3), and is the unconditional cost of obtaining one fresh valid instance flat or growing in the item's shortest-path hop distance - deciding whether persistent cross-episode state can buy a work reduction that grows with Web depth, or whether fresh-instance acquisition is a constant-cost procedure and effort should move to procedure caching and substrate expansion? The v1 freeze of this exact mandate (EXP-FRONTIER-37984242167) committed an empty sampling frame (0 seeds, 0 DEEP, 0 hosts, absent certificate, 0/0 falsifier). The first v2 draft (revision 1) selected hosts BECAUSE they published content-level sitemaps (selection-on-treatment / ceiling baseline) so SUPPORTS was near-certain by construction and FALSIFIES was structurally unreachable on the real pool, and two of its Sphinx hosts are now Cloudflare-429-challenged. Revisions 2 and 3 repair the sampling frame, the selection-on-treatment defect, the frame-exposing liveness control, the fragile hosts, and a fresh set of verifiability/satisfiability defects (unverifiable branch-exercise claim, exposure-blindness only by use, missing stability cap, missing engine-span requirement, undisclosed oracle channel, unformalised trend) before freeze.

question: Over the frozen exposure-blind multi-host pool in target_pool (493 admitted DEEP state-carrying pages: mdBook 485 on google.github.io / rust-lang.github.io / rustc-dev-guide.rust-lang.org, Sphinx 8 on pandas.pydata.org), confirmed during DESIGN by the frozen same-host static-<a> BFS (depth<=6, budget B=250) to contain DEEP (hop>=3) state-carrying pages on >=2 distinct generator engines and >=2 distinct hosts (ADMISSION_GATE_V2 PASS), what fraction of those admitted DEEP pages is reachable in <=K=3 fresh-agent GETs (up to 2 discovery GETs + 1 item-page GET) via ANY of the five frozen cold-start discovery channels (ROBOTS_SITEMAP, SITEMAP_XML, ON_SITE_SEARCH, RSS_ATOM, JSON_LD), with discovery matching under canonical resource identity (match_key: host + path with a single trailing '/', '.html', '.htm' removed)? And, descriptively, does reachability scale with hop? The preregistered materiality threshold 0.50 on >=2 distinct host units decides whether shortest-path hop is NOT a fundamental acquisition-cost barrier (discovery/substrate expansion, not path caching, is the target) versus fresh deep-instance acquisition remaining path-bound with a computable persistence break-even surface. The frame is EXPOSURE-BLIND: hosts are well-known documentation sites of widely-used open-source projects, screened BEFORE any discovery-surface inspection for credential-free stdlib crawlability (HTTP 200, no challenge) and DEEP topology (>=3 state-carrying pages at hop>=3 under the frozen same-host static-<a> BFS), with >=2 generator engines represented; no frame host's discovery surface (robots/sitemap/feed/JSON-LD/search) was inspected at DESIGN, so neither branch is pre-selected by construction. The pool is a convenience sample of that host class, so the inference is capability-bound and is disclosed as such.
hypothesis: H1 (SUPPORTS). On the exposure-blind frozen pool, site-native discovery reaches a material fraction (>=0.50) of admitted DEEP pages in <=K=3 GETs on >=2 distinct host units spanning >=2 generator engines. If H1 holds, shortest-path hop is NOT a fundamental acquisition-cost barrier for discovery-enabled acquisition on the frozen host class, path/procedure persistence is not the primary optimization target, and effort should move to discovery-channel coverage and substrate expansion. H0 (negative branch). Discovery reaches <0.50 of admitted DEEP pages on all but at most one host unit; then even with site-native discovery, fresh deep-instance acquisition remains path-bound and persistence of paths/procedures retains a measurable, depth-dependent amortization surface whose break-even can be computed from real re-derivation cost. The experiment does not presuppose which holds: the frame is exposure-blind by construction (link-only BFS parser), the pre-freeze certificate (spec.json.pre_freeze_control_certificate) shows both branches structurally reachable, and the reproducible --branch-drive mode drives the frozen code to SUPPORTS, MIXED (one host and single-engine) and FALSIFIES (no item-level reachability fraction is computed at DESIGN).

falsifier.unit: host unit = distinct registrable host of the seed's final root (per-engine grouping reported descriptively)
falsifier.positive_branch: SUPPORTS iff the number E of host units with discovery_reachable_fraction_per_host >= 0.50 is >= 2 AND those meeting hosts span >= 2 distinct generator engines (engines_meeting_threshold=true).
falsifier.mixed_branch: MIXED iff E >= 1 but not (E >= 2 with >= 2 engines among the meeting hosts): i.e. exactly one meeting host, OR >= 2 meeting hosts confined to a single engine.
falsifier.admission_gate: ADMISSION_GATE_V2: total admitted DEEP pages >= 10 AND >= 2 distinct generator engines with >= 3 admitted DEEP pages each AND >= 2 distinct hosts with >= 3 admitted DEEP pages each. Verified during DESIGN (493 >= 10; mdBook 485, Sphinx 8; 4 hosts >= 3) and re-evaluated at EXECUTE; failure -> status=MEASUREMENT_INVALID with the exact shortfall, never a scientific branch.
falsifier.per_channel_disclosure: Mandatory per-channel coverage discovery_reachable_fraction_per_channel[channel]; any channel yielding zero admitted DEEP items is explicitly listed as a zero channel, not treated as null.
falsifier.arithmetic_realizability: The denominator (number of admitted DEEP pages) is 493 (>= 10 by construction) and the per-host fraction lies in [0,1], so E in {0,1,2,3,4} is well-defined and every branch is arithmetically reachable. The local stdlib fixtures CAL_DISCOVERABLE_FIXTURE (fraction 1.0) and CAL_OPAQUE_FIXTURE (fraction 0.0) bracket the 0.50 boundary from both sides, demonstrating that the instrument can produce both a passing and a failing host unit; and the frozen --branch-drive mode re-uses the real compute_metrics/decide path to reach SUPPORTS (E>=2, engines_ok), MIXED (one host), MIXED (>=2 hosts on a single engine), FALSIFIES (E==0), admission-gate failure, calibration failure, empty denominator and the stability cap, emitting branch_drive.json with all_branches_reachable=true (DESIGN observation: PASS). Because the frame is exposure-blind BY CONSTRUCTION (the link-only StaticLinks BFS parser has no discovery fields), neither E==0 nor E>=2 is foreclosed by construction. This repairs revision 1, in which hosts were selected for exposing content-level sitemaps so E>=2 was near-certain and E==0 was structurally unreachable on the real pool. No item-level reachability fraction was computed at DESIGN; attainability is argued structurally and by the frozen branch drive instead.

what_each_branch_means.SUPPORTS: shortest-path hop is not a fundamental acquisition-cost barrier for discovery-enabled acquisition on the frozen host class; discovery and substrate expansion are the optimization target; persistent path caching is de-prioritized with recorded evidence. Requires >= 2 host units across >= 2 engines. Bounded to the identified host class (section 12 of prereg.md); no Web-wide prevalence claim.
what_each_branch_means.FALSIFIES: fresh deep-instance acquisition remains path-bound even with site-native discovery on this host class; persistent paths/procedures retain a computable, depth-dependent amortization surface and the break-even can be derived from the recorded re-derivation cost.
what_each_branch_means.MIXED: the cross-host/cross-engine contrast is split (exactly one host, or >= 2 hosts on a single engine); no program-level decision change and the next experiment must resolve discovery-channel coverage or frame composition.

baselines.role: comparator (link-following re-derivation); supplies the hop depth and the cumulative GET/byte cost of the item-blind same-host BFS up to each admitted DEEP page
baselines.policy: frozen item-blind same-host BFS from the seed root, document order, budget B=250, depth cap D=6 (this experiment's pool-construction pass)
baselines.expected: >= hop+1 for every admitted page (detour-free chain is the degenerate equality case)

baselines.role: re-acquisition via persisted shortest path (inherited from EXP-FRONTIER-37950626378)
baselines.policy: GET each node on the frozen shortest path seed -> ... -> item page in hop order; cost = hop+1 GETs
baselines.expected: near-linear in hop; strictly cheaper than B_LINK_FOLLOWING_BFS whenever the BFS takes a detour

baselines.policy: one GET to the known item page URL
CAL_OPAQUE_FIXTURE: a local stdlib site with the same deep structure but no robots/sitemap/feed/search/JSON-LD; discovery must yield 0

positive_control.description: Composite Step-0 gate. (a) apparatus liveness on OUT-OF-POOL hosts: at least one frozen discovery channel (ROBOTS_SITEMAP/SITEMAP_XML) fetches and parses >= 1 URL on >= 1 host of LIVE_PROBE_HOSTS, which are disjoint from the frame seeds; (b) PC_HOP_CONFIRMATION: a preregistered true-hop-1 page must be recovered by the frozen BFS; (c) PC_SEED_HOST_IDENTITY: every seed's final root must stay on its declared host; (d) PC_LIVE_PROBE_LIVENESS at EXECUTE. Because liveness is proven away from the frame, a genuine frame-wide FALSIFIES is never converted into MEASUREMENT_INVALID.
positive_control.pass_criterion: (a) at least one of ROBOTS_SITEMAP / SITEMAP_XML fetches and parses >= 1 URL on >= 1 out-of-pool probe host (LIVE_PROBE_HOSTS), verified live during DESIGN with evidence in pre_freeze_control_certificate; AND (b) the frozen BFS returns found==true with hop==1 for the preregistered target https://google.github.io/comprehensive-rust/android.html; AND (c) PC_SEED_HOST_IDENTITY: every seed's final_root netloc equals its declared host (no cross-host redirect re-basing a probe); AND (d) PC_LIVE_PROBE_LIVENESS at EXECUTE. Criterion (a)/(d) is deliberately phrased on parsed-URL liveness on out-of-frame hosts, NOT on admitting a specific DEEP item from a frame host, so a genuine FALSIFIES remains reachable and is not masked as MEASUREMENT_INVALID.
positive_control.evidence_required: HTTP status, content-type and parsed entry count per verified channel per out-of-pool host; hop observed for the true-hop-1 target; declared vs final_root host per seed; per-probe-host parsed-URL count (urls_count) at EXECUTE.

null_control.description: Synthetic item URLs that do not exist, probed through every discovery channel. A channel must yield zero reachable items, and the synthetic item page must be non-2xx. Run on out-of-pool probe hosts at DESIGN (to preserve frame exposure-blindness) and on the pool hosts at EXECUTE inside the frozen code.
null_control.pass_criterion: For each of the 5 channels, the synthetic probe returns success == false (0 reachable URLs).
null_control.purpose: Validates that discovery channels do not produce false-positive reachability via search suggestions, redirect chains or parser errors, including under canonical match_key matching.

measurement_validity.rule: Credential-free GET-only stdlib HTTP (urllib + http.server for local fixtures). No browser, JS, Docker, model key, credential, cookie, write verb or tokenizer. GET = one logical request with followed redirects; a separate redirect/validation fetch consumes the K spare.

The seed list is frozen at DESIGN in target_pool.seeds; EXECUTE re-runs the frozen BFS (depth<=6, budget 250) to reconstruct the pool and re-applies ADMISSION_GATE_V2. If the live pool no longer satisfies the gate, status=MEASUREMENT_INVALID with the exact shortfall; the cross-engine contrast is never reported as FLAT from an empty or single-engine frame.

Five frozen cold-start channels: (1) ROBOTS_SITEMAP: GET /robots.txt -> Sitemap: directives -> GET sitemap(s) -> parse <loc> or plain-text URL lines; (2) SITEMAP_XML: GET /sitemap.xml, /sitemap_index.xml, /sitemap-index.xml directly -> parse; (3) ON_SITE_SEARCH: GET the seed root, locate a server-side search form/action, GET action?name=<item path segment>, parse result links; (4) RSS_ATOM: GET the seed root, follow a <link rel=alternate type=application/rss+xml|atom+xml>, parse entry links; (5) JSON_LD: GET the seed root (a cold hub resource, never the item page), parse application/ld+json and collect url/@id/mainEntityOfPage/contentUrl values. All channels are cold-start: the item page is fetched only AFTER the item URL is discovered.

Discovery matching uses canonical resource identity match_key(host, path) with a single trailing '/', '.html' or '.htm' removed (frozen in run.py). A sitemap may list the canonical spelling ('/component/button') while static links use '.html'; both denote the same resource, so canonical matching measures whether the page was enumerated rather than whether one particular spelling was enumerated. Pool building/dedup keeps exact URLs. Guards against false merges: item page must return 2xx; NC_SYNTHETIC_UNREACHABLE_ITEM; per-host/per-channel disclosure. Applied only inside the discovery step, never to pool identity.

K=3 total GETs per item per channel = up to DISCOVERY_GETS_MAX=2 discovery GETs + exactly 1 item-page GET. A channel succeeds for an item iff the item URL is discovered within the discovery budget (matched under match_key) AND the item page returns a 2xx status within K. Sitemap-index recursion or multi-sitemap fetches beyond 2 discovery GETs do not count as success.

Shortest-path hop for each admitted page is computed by the SAME frozen same-host static-<a> BFS (document order, budget 250, depth 6) used to build the pool. Hop and discovery reachability are distinct observables measured on the same item set.

Each channel is probed independently with its own fresh budget. An item counts as reachable if ANY channel succeeds. Per-channel coverage is reported separately and a zero-yield channel is explicitly listed.
No tokenizer, latency timer or dollar-cost model. GET request count and response-body bytes are the only cost bases; token fields are null.

Stdlib html.parser only. Only static <a href>, <form>/<input>/<select> (named controls), <link rel=alternate rss/atom> and <script type=application/ld+json> are detectable. JS-rendered navigation, JS search indexes (e.g. mdBook searchindex.js, Sphinx client search) and JS-injected JSON-LD are missed and disclosed as representation loss. This is conservative for SUPPORTS: rich hosts could have even more JS-mediated discovery that this instrument does not credit.

The pre-freeze control certificate (spec.json.pre_freeze_control_certificate) must be all_verified=true with live evidence before freeze: (a) pool admits DEEP pages on >=2 engines and >=2 hosts; (b) out-of-pool channel liveness verified; (c) null control yields 0 reachable; (f) all falsifier branches structurally reachable (instrument range bracketed by fixtures; frame exposure-blind by construction; the frozen --branch-drive mode drives the real decision path to SUPPORTS, MIXED (one host), MIXED (single engine), FALSIFIES, gate failure, empty denominator and the stability cap). No item-level reachability fraction is computed at DESIGN. This experiment's DESIGN satisfied all (see certificate).
Each item-channel probe is a fresh episode (no cross-item caching of discovered URLs within the experiment). This measures fresh-agent acquisition cost, not amortized multi-item discovery.

Session 1 measures every admitted DEEP item under the frozen policy. Session 2 re-measures a deterministic 25% subsample (sha256(item_id) mod 4 == 0). An item is flagged unstable iff its per-channel success vector differs between sessions; unstable items are excluded from the decision denominator with the unstable list recorded. exclusion_fraction = n_unstable_excluded / n_subsample. STABILITY_CAP: if exclusion_fraction > MAX_EXCLUSION_FRACTION (0.10) the run is MEASUREMENT_INVALID, so rate-limit-induced denominator erosion cannot silently inflate or deflate the per-host fraction. n_unstable_excluded, unstable_items, stability_subsample_size, stability_subsample_fraction_session_1/_session_2 and exclusion_fraction are all reported.

If a seed host is unreachable at EXECUTE time, record status=BLOCKED and the exact error; network failure is never encoded as a scientific branch. DESIGN confirmed all four seed hosts reachable without challenge and the out-of-pool channel-liveness certificate on 2026-10-11. Revision 1's Cloudflare-429-challenged Sphinx hosts are deliberately excluded.

The admitted item unit is the state-carrying PAGE (page_url with >=1 named <input>/<select>), item_id = sha256(host + '|' + page_url). This resolves a v1 ambiguity: control-level tuples over-weight engines with many named controls per page. Control-level tuples are reported descriptively only.

A page reachable from multiple seeds is admitted once at its minimum same-host static-hop, attributed to the seed giving that minimum hop (ties broken by lexicographically smallest seed), attributed to the host/engine of the winning seed's final root. In the final pool no two seeds share a host.

JSON_LD is a cold-start channel: structured data is read from the seed root (or another discovery-obtained hub), never from the item page. A site that exposes JSON-LD only on the item page earns no JSON_LD credit; self-referential item-page JSON-LD is disclosed, not scored.

The frame is EXPOSURE-BLIND BY CONSTRUCTION. The frame BFS parser is `StaticLinks`, which extracts only static `<a href>` and has NO feeds/search_forms/jsonld fields at all; therefore no discovery-surface field can be produced, recorded, printed or used in any DESIGN decision even in principle. Hosts are well-known documentation sites of widely-used open-source projects, screened before any discovery-surface inspection for reachability (HTTP 200, no challenge) and DEEP topology (>=3 state-carrying pages at hop>=3 under the frozen BFS), with >=2 generator engines represented. Instrument liveness is verified on local stdlib fixtures and on out-of-pool LIVE_PROBE_HOSTS that are disjoint from SEEDS. Consequently neither SUPPORTS nor FALSIFIES is pre-determined by host selection, and a frame-wide zero is a genuine scientific FALSIFIES. The frame is a convenience sample of the documentation-site class; the claim is capability-bound and no Web-wide prevalence estimate is made. (In revision 2 the topology parser reused the general HTMLScan and exposure-blindness was a promise about which fields were *used*; revision 3 replaces it with the link-only parser so the property is structural and auditable. The regenerated frame is topologically identical: 493 DEEP, 197/94/194/8.)

PC_SEED_HOST_IDENTITY: for every frozen seed, the final redirect root's netloc must equal the declared host. A cross-host redirect would silently re-base the discovery probe on a different site and invalidate every per-host fraction; a mismatch is a Step-0 failure (status=MEASUREMENT_INVALID), never a scientific branch. Verified at DESIGN (all four match) and re-checked inside the frozen confirmatory code.

CALIBRATION_GATE: confirmatory() re-runs the local dynamic-range calibration (discoverable fixture == 1.0, opaque fixture == 0.0) in-process before any measurement and short-circuits to status=MEASUREMENT_INVALID / outcome=INCONCLUSIVE if it fails. The `--calibrate` CLI mode exists for the EXECUTE log, but the gate is self-enforcing and does not depend on process sequencing.

SITEMAP_XML enumerates at most the first DISCOVERY_GETS_MAX=2 of the fixed candidate list (/sitemap.xml, /sitemap_index.xml, /sitemap-index.xml); the third path is reached only if an earlier candidate did not consume the budget. This is deterministic and disclosed; a missing third-path enumeration is never interpreted as absence.

SUPPORTS requires not only E >= 2 host units meeting 0.50 but also that those meeting hosts span >= 2 distinct generator engines (engines_meeting_threshold). E >= 2 confined to a single engine is MIXED. This formalises the mandate's 'materiality on >=2 host/engine units' and blocks a single-engine mdBook-heavy frame from reading as a cross-engine SUPPORTS.

STABILITY_CAP = 0.10. Session 2 re-measures a deterministic 25% subsample; if the inter-session exclusion fraction exceeds 0.10 the run is status=MEASUREMENT_INVALID / outcome=INCONCLUSIVE (never a scientific branch). Bounds rate-limit/throttling-induced denominator erosion. DESIGN exercised the cap at exclusion 0.25 (branch_drive.json stability_cap fires).
Every non-localhost GET is preceded by a PACE_S=0.15 s sleep (localhost fixtures exempt) to reduce transient throttling on hosts with up to 197 admitted items under per-item fresh budgets (VN-V10).

The frame BFS parser `StaticLinks` exposes only static `<a href>` resolution and has no discovery fields; exposure-blindness is therefore a structural property of the parser object, not a promise about field usage. Verified by the regenerated frame being topologically identical to the recorded one.

ON_SITE_SEARCH derives its query from the last path segment of the KNOWN item URL, so it is oracle-like and cannot stand alone as evidence of cold-start discovery. It is disclosed, per-channel coverage is reported, and the code additionally emits discovery_reachable_fraction_per_host_without_on_site_search and oracle_dependent_supports so the decision can be read with and without this channel.

flat_vs_growing_trend is computed by a frozen rule: FALLING iff frac(reachable | hop>=5) < frac(reachable | hop=3) - TREND_DROP(0.10) with >= TREND_MIN_BUCKET(5) items in each bucket; FLAT iff not FALLING and both buckets are large enough; UNMEASURED if any bucket has fewer than 5 items. The rule is descriptive and does not enter the primary decision. DESIGN pool deep_by_hop = {3:242,4:175,5:56,6:20}, so both buckets exceed the minimum.

primary.discovery_reachable_fraction: count(admitted DEEP pages with any_success) / count(admitted DEEP pages)
primary.discovery_reachable_fraction_per_host[ho: same fraction computed per distinct host (decision unit)
primary.discovery_reachable_fraction_per_engine[: same fraction computed per generator engine (mdBook / Sphinx), descriptive

secondary.discovery_reachable_fraction_per_channel: fraction of admitted DEEP pages reachable via that channel alone
secondary.discovery_reachable_fraction_by_hop[3..6: hop-stratified reachability (path-bound vs flat diagnostic); reported with n_by_hop
secondary.n_by_hop: number of admitted DEEP items per hop bucket (bucket-size disclosure for the trend rule)
secondary.flat_vs_growing_trend: frozen diagnostic object {label, frac_hop3, frac_hop_ge5, n_hop3, n_hop_ge5} per VN-V25
secondary.discovery_reachable_fraction_per_host_wi: oracle-free per-host sensitivity (excludes the oracle-like ON_SITE_SEARCH channel)
secondary.oracle_dependent_supports: hosts that meet 0.50 only when ON_SITE_SEARCH is included
secondary.median_discovery_gets_reachable: median total GETs among successful channel probes
secondary.host_units_meeting_threshold: E = number of HOST units with per-host fraction >= 0.50 (the decision unit is the distinct host), NOT a count of engines
secondary.engines_meeting_threshold: boolean; true iff the E meeting host units span >= 2 distinct generator engines (required for SUPPORTS, VN-V20)
secondary.exclusion_fraction: n_unstable_excluded / stability_subsample_size; STABILITY_CAP fails the run above 0.10
secondary.n_unstable_excluded: items with inter-session channel-vector disagreement, excluded from the decision denominator
secondary.unstable_items: list of excluded item ids (path/url) with reason
secondary.stability_subsample_size: size of the deterministic 25% session-2 subsample
secondary.stability_subsample_fraction_session_1: session-1 pooled reachability fraction restricted to the subsample
secondary.stability_subsample_fraction_session_2: session-2 pooled reachability fraction on the subsample
secondary.cost_baselines: measured cost baselines over the same admitted item set, with frozen ids (see baselines[]): median_bfs_gets (B_LINK_FOLLOWING_BFS, cumulative GETs to first reach each admitted page, captured as per-item bfs_cost), median_persisted_path_gets (B_PERSISTED_PATH_REACQUISITION, hop+1), median_direct_replay_gets (B_DIRECT_URL_REPLAY, 1), and median/mean discovery GETs on success; also cost_by_hop (per-hop medians) as the flat-vs-growing diagnostic. These make the baselines emitted measurements rather than prose.

metrics.controls_metric: controls.<id>.pass for PC_DISCOVERY_CHANNEL_REACHABILITY, PC_LIVE_PROBE_LIVENESS, PC_SEED_HOST_IDENTITY, PC_HOP_CONFIRMATION, NC_SYNTHETIC_UNREACHABLE_ITEM, STABILITY_CAP, CAL_DISCOVERABLE_FIXTURE, CAL_OPAQUE_FIXTURE, CALIBRATION_GATE, ADMISSION_GATE

resolved_design_decisions.final_seed_list: 4 frozen exposure-blind seeds: google.github.io/comprehensive-rust/ (mdBook), rust-lang.github.io/async-book/ (mdBook), rustc-dev-guide.rust-lang.org/ (mdBook), pandas.pydata.org/docs/ (Sphinx). No stratum.
resolved_design_decisions.frame_selection_rule: Exposure-blind: well-known documentation hosts of widely-used open-source projects, screened BEFORE any discovery-surface inspection for credential-free stdlib crawlability (HTTP 200, no challenge) and DEEP topology (>=3 state-carrying pages at hop>=3 under the frozen BFS), with >=2 generator engines represented. Revision 1's 5 hosts and the v1 frame are excluded. No frame host discovery surface was fetched, recorded or used at DESIGN.
resolved_design_decisions.canonical_discovery_matching: match_key(u) = (netloc.lower(), path with one trailing '/', '.html' or '.htm' removed). Applied only to discovery matching (channel enumerated URLs vs admitted item URL); pool identity keeps exact URLs.
resolved_design_decisions.synthetic_identifier_format: spider-nonexistent-38085197666-<a|b>.html appended to a host; expected 0 reachable and non-2xx item page.
resolved_design_decisions.search_query_parameter_mapping: Use the named control on the located search form (via_input name) or 'q' default; query value = last path segment of the item URL with a trailing .html/.php/.htm/.asp/.aspx stripped; discovery GETs capped at 2.
resolved_design_decisions.json_ld_vocabulary: Collect 'url', '@id', 'mainEntityOfPage', 'contentUrl', 'sameAs' from any @graph/ItemList/WebPage/BreadcrumbList/SearchAction objects; cold-start only (seed root hub).
resolved_design_decisions.sitemap_gz_handling: sitemap files are read as fetched text; if a response is gzip-encoded and not transparently decoded by urllib, the channel records 0 entries (disclosed). Plain-text sitemaps (one URL per line) and XML <loc> sitemaps are both parsed.
resolved_design_decisions.redirect_accounting: One logical GET with redirects followed counts as 1; a separate validation GET, if issued, consumes the K spare. Channels never exceed DISCOVERY_GETS_MAX discovery GETs.
resolved_design_decisions.engine_definition: Generator engine fingerprint: mdBook (google.github.io/comprehensive-rust, rust-lang.github.io/async-book, rustc-dev-guide.rust-lang.org) vs Sphinx (pandas.pydata.org/docs). The decision unit is the distinct host; engine grouping is reported descriptively AND enforced for SUPPORTS via engines_meeting_threshold (>=2 engines among the meeting hosts, VN-V20).
resolved_design_decisions.item_unit: State-carrying page (>=1 named <input>/<select>); item_id = sha256(host + '|' + page_url); control-level tuples supplementary (VN-V13).

decision_rule: Frozen, evaluated in order. Step 0 controls: run CALIBRATION_GATE (discoverable fixture fraction 1.0 AND opaque fixture 0.0, re-enabled in-process inside confirmatory()), PC_HOP_CONFIRMATION (expect found & hop 1, read from the recorded frame pass so no redundant crawl is issued), PC_SEED_HOST_IDENTITY (final_root host == declared host for every seed), NC_SYNTHETIC_UNREACHABLE_ITEM (expect 0 reachable across all pool hosts x 5 channels x 2 synthetic ids), PC_LIVE_PROBE_LIVENESS (expect >= 1 OUT-OF-POOL probe host where ROBOTS_SITEMAP/SITEMAP_XML fetch and parse >= 1 URL; apparatus liveness, independent of the frame so FALSIFIES stays reachable), STABILITY_CAP (expect exclusion_fraction <= 0.10). Any control failure -> status=MEASUREMENT_INVALID, outcome=INCONCLUSIVE (infrastructure/substrate failure, never a scientific answer). Step 1 admission: reconstruct the pool from the frozen seeds under the frozen BFS; apply ADMISSION_GATE_V2; failure -> status=MEASUREMENT_INVALID with exact shortfall. Step 2 measurement: session 1 measures every admitted DEEP page x 5 channels within K=3 under match_key; session 2 re-measures a deterministic 25% subsample; drop items with inter-session disagreement (VN-V11) and fail if exclusion_fraction > 0.10 (VN-V21). Step 3: compute discovery_reachable_fraction (pooled), per-host, per-engine, per-channel, by-hop (with n_by_hop), the trend object, and the cost_baselines; E = number of HOST units with per-host fraction >= 0.50; engines_ok = the E meeting hosts span >= 2 engines. Outcome: SUPPORTS iff E >= 2 AND engines_ok (status=COMPLETE); MIXED iff E >= 1 otherwise; FALSIFIES iff E == 0. Every terminal path (calibration failure, gate failure, Step-0 failure, or a COMPLETE run) writes the full artifact triple result.json + report.md + provenance.json via write_terminal(); the report's Status/Outcome line is derived from the final status_final/outcome_final, never from the pre-control branch. No outcome is recorded as a failure; only genuine measurement invalidity is MEASUREMENT_INVALID.
product_consequence_positive: If SUPPORTS: shortest-path hop is not a fundamental acquisition-cost barrier for discovery-enabled acquisition on the frozen documentation host class; SPIDER should optimize discovery-channel coverage and substrate expansion rather than path/procedure caching. C-CROSSSITE gains a bounded positive that a reusable discovery procedure transfers across >=2 host units (not a Web-wide prevalence claim). Freshness (C-FRESHNESS) and delta-repair become lower priority for the acquisition phase. No mechanism is promoted to Product Core by this experiment.
product_consequence_negative: If FALSIFIES: even with site-native discovery, fresh deep-instance acquisition remains path-bound on this host class; persistence of paths/procedures retains a measurable depth-dependent amortization surface and the break-even reuse count can be computed from the recorded re-derivation cost. SPIDER's memory architecture should continue investing in path/procedure persistence with freshness guards. If MIXED: no program-level decision change; the next experiment must resolve discovery-channel coverage or frame composition.
estimated_cost: DESIGN already paid: pool-construction BFS (observed 976 page GETs across 4 seeds: 250+250+226+250) plus out-of-pool channel-liveness/null/calibration/branch probes. EXECUTE: pool reconstruction <=1000 GETs; session 1 = 493 admitted pages x 5 channels x <=3 GETs (~<=7395 GETs) + session 2 on a deterministic 25% subsample (~<=1849 GETs) + calibration/controls; wall time target <= 60 min with PACE_S=0.15. Stdlib only; no browser, Docker, key, credential, cookie or tokenizer.
expected_information_gain: High. The question was left entirely unmeasured by v1 (empty frame, 0/0 falsifier), and revision 1's frame pre-determined SUPPORTS (selection-on-treatment) and was fragile to Cloudflare. This revision is the first measurement on a genuinely exposure-blind, multi-engine/multi-host DEEP pool, so a SUPPORTS is not a construction artifact and a FALSIFIES is not structurally foreclosed. Genuinely uncertain content: (i) whether site-native discovery of the frozen documentation hosts enumerates their DEEP pages at all (mdBook and Sphinx hosts frequently publish no content-level sitemap); (ii) whether any host crosses 0.50; (iii) the flat-vs-growing cost_baselines diagnostic; (iv) per-channel coverage. Both directions still change a program-level architecture decision (discovery/substrate expansion vs path/procedure persistence), bounded by host class.

decision_rule_reachability.reason: The denominator (admitted DEEP pages) is 493 (>= 10) by the frozen pool (gate PASS) and the per-host fraction lies in [0,1], so E (hosts meeting 0.50) is well-defined in {0,...,4} and SUPPORTS (E>=2 with engines_ok), MIXED (one host, or >=2 hosts on one engine) and FALSIFIES (E==0) are all arithmetically reachable. Two local stdlib fixtures bracket the 0.50 boundary from both sides (1.0 discoverable, 0.0 opaque). Crucially, with the frozen section-13 code, every status/outcome path was exercised end-to-end by the reproducible --branch-drive mode and each wrote a consistent result/report/provenance triple: SUPPORTS (E>=2, engines_ok), MIXED (one host), MIXED (single engine), FALSIFIES (E==0), admission-gate failure, calibration failure, empty denominator and the stability cap. The frame is EXPOSURE-BLIND BY CONSTRUCTION (the link-only StaticLinks BFS parser has no discovery fields), so neither branch is pre-selected. The v1 defect (0/0 denominator) and the revision-1 defect (selection-on-treatment, E>=2 near-certain / E==0 unreachable on the real pool) cannot recur because the exposure-blind frame is constructed, verified and recorded in the frozen packet before freeze; no item-level reachability fraction is computed at DESIGN.

measurement_prerequisites.reason: All prerequisites were probed live during DESIGN on the same runner class (bare CPython, network enabled): (a) all four pool hosts reachable over TLS (HTTP 200 on the seed roots) with final_root host == declared host (PC_SEED_HOST_IDENTITY PASS, no cross-host redirect, no Cloudflare challenge); (b) the frozen BFS built the 493-page DEEP pool within B=250/D=6 (4 hosts, 2 engines, gate PASS) and the reconstruction was repeated on a fresh build with identical counts; (c) at least one discovery channel (ROBOTS_SITEMAP/SITEMAP_XML) is live and parsable on five OUT-OF-POOL probe hosts disjoint from the frame; (d) the null control yields zero reachable; (e) the full pipeline runs end-to-end on local stdlib fixtures, and every status/outcome path executes without crashing (spec.json.design_repairs_and_satisfiability). Substrate is stdlib-only; no browser, model, key or credential is required.

baseline_identifiability.reason: Four stable, mutually distinct baselines with deterministic policies: B_LINK_FOLLOWING_BFS (item-blind same-host BFS, >= hop+1 GETs), B_PERSISTED_PATH_REACQUISITION (hop+1 GETs), B_DIRECT_URL_REPLAY (1 GET) and B_NO_DISCOVERY (0.0 floor on CAL_OPAQUE_FIXTURE). The treatment (discovery reachability) is a distinct decision function over the same admitted item set, so the discovery-vs-link-following contrast is identified. Identities are frozen in spec.json baselines[] and prereg section 5 and are reused verbatim by EXECUTE/AUDIT.

control_sensitivity.reason: Every control can fire in both directions and no Step-0 control is correlated with the treatment: CAL_DISCOVERABLE_FIXTURE and CAL_OPAQUE_FIXTURE prove the instrument yields 1.0 and 0.0, and CALIBRATION_GATE re-enforces this in-process before measurement; PC_HOP_CONFIRMATION fails loudly if hop computation is broken (it reads the recorded frame pass, so it does not add a redundant crawl); PC_SEED_HOST_IDENTITY fails loudly if a seed's final root leaves its declared host (cross-host redirect); PC_LIVE_PROBE_LIVENESS fails loudly if the sitemap/robots channels fetch/parse nothing on out-of-pool probe hosts at EXECUTE but keys on parsed-URL count, not on admitting a DEEP item from a frame host, so a genuine FALSIFIES is not converted into MEASUREMENT_INVALID; NC_SYNTHETIC_UNREACHABLE_ITEM catches false-positive discovery via search suggestions/redirects/parser error; STABILITY_CAP fails loudly when inter-session instability exceeds 0.10, so throttle-induced denominator erosion is caught rather than averaged in; ADMISSION_GATE fails loudly if the live pool collapses. The 0.50 materiality threshold is strictly between the two live-measured calibration endpoints. No post-hoc reweighting is permitted.

treatment_liveness.reason: The treatment (the five site-native discovery channels) is not an empty shell: the complete discovery pipeline executed end-to-end during DESIGN on local stdlib fixtures and produced fraction 1.0 (via ROBOTS_SITEMAP/SITEMAP_XML) and 0.0 (opaque); the frozen ROBOTS_SITEMAP/SITEMAP_XML machinery fetched and parsed >= 1 URL on five out-of-pool probe hosts (--live-probe); and the --branch-drive mode shows the decision path can reach SUPPORTS/MIXED/FALSIFIES. Because the frame is exposure-blind by construction, whether the treatment succeeds on a frame host is exactly what EXECUTE measures; the instrument demonstrably can both succeed and fail. No confirmatory item-level outcome was computed at DESIGN: the out-of-pool liveness probe records only that the channel machinery is operational on the live Web (an apparatus fact recorded on non-frame hosts). EXECUTE re-measures authoritatively under the frozen protocol.

freeze_artifacts_bound.reason: There is no mutable local file, task bank, dataset or fixture whose identity can change the interpretation. The frozen seed list (host + engine), the BFS policy, the link-only StaticLinks parser, the five channel definitions, canonical match_key, K accounting, admission gate, metrics and decision rule are all inlined in spec.json, and the COMPLETE outcome-bearing code (pool construction, discovery channels, out-of-pool liveness probe, null control, calibration fixtures, branch drive, metrics, decision) is frozen VERBATIM inside prereg.md section 13, which freeze.json hashes transitively; EXECUTE must reproduce it byte-for-byte and verify CODE_SHA256 before running. The only remote dependency is the live public Web (an external network resource, not a mutable local artifact), pinned by the frozen seed list and re-checked by ADMISSION_GATE_V2 at EXECUTE. Per EXPERIMENT_PACKET.md section 2, when no mutable local dependency exists freeze_artifacts_bound must be NOT_APPLICABLE with a reason and the list is empty; the DESIGN-stage write restriction (scripts/check_scope.py: DESIGN may only write spec.json/prereg.md) makes pre-freeze artifact files impossible by construction, and the prereg-embedded code is strictly stronger (hash-bound).
